title: Pectoralis Minor Length Test
purpose: Muscle length test for tightness of the pectoralis minor, a muscle that shortens with prolonged desk posture (protracted shoulders, arms in internal rotation and adduction).
structure: Pectoralis minor (coracoid process to ribs 3-5); scapular protraction and anterior tilt.
procedure: Patient supine. The examiner places the heels of the hands on both coracoid processes and applies downward (posterior) pressure.
positive: A muscle-stretch sensation reported by the patient indicates pectoralis minor tightness.
notes: The page gives no normal reference (e.g. coracoid height from the table) and no reliability data. The video embed starts at 66 s of a longer video (t=66). Related length tests: pectoralis major, biceps brachii, triceps brachii. Source files this under 'Chest Assessment'.

title: Biceps Brachii Length Test
purpose: Muscle length test for the biceps brachii, a tonic muscle that tends to tighten; it flexes, abducts and internally rotates the shoulder and flexes and supinates the elbow.
structure: Biceps brachii across the shoulder and elbow (both heads).
procedure: Patient supine with the shoulder extended (arm off the end of the table), the elbow flexed and the forearm supinated. The examiner extends the elbow.
positive: Normal: full elbow extension with a bone-to-bone end-feel. Positive: elbow extension cannot be completed and the patient feels a muscular stretch.
notes: Janda-type classification (tonic muscle). No reliability or accuracy data. Related: pectoralis major, pectoralis minor and triceps length tests. Source files this under 'Shoulder & Elbow Assessment'; placed in shoulder because shoulder extension sets the stretch.

title: Triceps Brachii Length Test
purpose: Muscle length test for the triceps brachii, a phasic muscle (Janda) that tends to weaken when underused; it extends and adducts the shoulder and extends the elbow.
structure: Triceps brachii, especially the long head across the shoulder.
procedure: Patient sitting with the arm fully forward flexed and in lateral rotation. The examiner stabilises the humerus and flexes the patient's elbow.
positive: Normal: elbow flexion ends with soft tissue approximation between the biceps and the forearm. Positive: elbow flexion is limited and the end-feel is muscle stretch.
notes: No reliability or accuracy data. Related: pectoralis major, pectoralis minor and biceps length tests. Source files this under 'Shoulder & Elbow Assessment'; placed in shoulder because full shoulder flexion sets the stretch.
